name: Scenario 1: Simple greeting
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. I’m Amina, your community health worker. How can I help you today? If you have any health concerns, please share.

name: Scenario 2: Emergency — chest pain
response_text:
EMERGENCY ALERT

This sounds like a medical emergency. Please act immediately:

1. CALL 199 (Ambulance) NOW
2. Or go directly to: EFSTH Emergency (Banjul) - 15min drive - Call 199
3. Sit upright, stay calm, chew aspirin if available. Do NOT lie flat.

Watch for: This may be: Possible heart attack. Every minute counts.

If someone is with you, have them call while you prepare to leave.
Stay strong — help is on the way.

name: Scenario 3: Emergency — stroke signs
response_text:

Stay strong — help is on the way.

name: Scenario 5: High BP 160/100
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. Your blood pressure is high at 160/100. Start taking 5mg of amlodipine daily. Reduce salt in your food, like cutting one Maggi cube from your domoda. Check your blood pressure again in 3 days. If it stays high, visit Kerewan health post that same day.

name: Scenario 6: Detailed symptom -> triage without form nudge
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. Your headache sounds bothersome. Rest for the next 2 days and drink 2 glasses of water every hour. If it doesn't go away or gets worse, contact your CHW. Is there anything else bothering you?

name: Scenario 7: Vague symptom -> form CTA
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. I’m sorry you have a headache. Rest now and drink two glasses of water. Monitor how you feel. How long have you had this headache? If it lasts more than three days, contact your CHW. If you want me to assess this more precisely, tap the Symptom button to fill a short form.

name: Scenario 8: Vague prescription -> form CTA
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. What is the name of the medication the doctor gave you? How much should you take, and how often? This will help me give you the right advice. If it's easier, you can tap Upload Rx to send a photo, or tap Rx to fill in the details.

name: Scenario 9: Detailed Rx -> specific guidance
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. You should take your Metformin 500mg with food, twice daily for 30 days. Aim for a fasting sugar level between 70 and 130 mg/dL. Watch for any unusual dizziness or low energy. Have you been checking your blood sugar regularly?

name: Scenario 10: Permission barrier -> Alkallo
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. It's common for families to make health decisions together. Talk to the Alkallo or a trusted elder first. Ask them to support your visit to the clinic. Plan for a day that suits your family's routine. If you feel unwell, check your blood pressure. What's your husband's main concern about the clinic?

name: Scenario 11: Stigma barrier -> community support
details: suggest_community_support_tool=True, response_excerpt=salaam aleikum. iwurara! welcome. welcome. it's okay to feel ashamed, but many p
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. It's okay to feel ashamed, but many people have diabetes. You can manage it. Start by eating less sugar and more vegetables. Walk for 30 minutes each day. If you feel very tired or dizzy, come to Kerewan health post. Have you talked to anyone about your diabetes?

name: Scenario 12: Cost barrier
response_text: Salaam aleikum. Iwurara! Welcome. Welcome. I understand money is tight. Ask your CHW: "What NCD services are free at my nearest health post?" Many medications like amlodipine are often cheap or free. Also, check if there’s a community support group in your village. When did you last check your blood pressure?

response_text: It's great to hear that you're staying active by walking sometimes and enjoying your favorite dish, benachin. While you haven't mentioned any specific concerns or symptoms, maintaining your health with hypertension and diabetes is important.
